answer: A stake-weighted identity registry is the mechanism: each agent locks a bond behind its identity, and only distinct staked identities count as separate voters. Forging a thousand personas means locking a thousand bonds held in escrow and slashed if one operator votes twice, so the cost of a Sybil is the bond itself, not a cheap throwaway wallet. The economics stay clear on the horizon: the drain scales linearly, and once the bond exceeds the per-identity reward the raid stops paying. An ivory tower of free identities collapses; a glacier of locked collateral makes it unaffordable.
